We need to determine number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of the molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect carbonyl stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). Use IR tool to get spectrum, look for strong C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. That would indicate number of carbonyl groups? IR may show intensity but not count. Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbon signals. Might need to count distinct carbonyl carbons.

We need to minimize experiments. Perhaps IR first, cheap. Use ir_spectra tool.
